title: Short Stuff: When Elvis Met Nixon
summary: Short Stuff episode on the December 21, 1970 meeting between Elvis Presley and President Richard Nixon at the White House. Drawing on a 2010 Smithsonian magazine article by Peter Carlson, the hosts recount how Elvis wrote a letter requesting federal agent credentials, flew from Los Angeles to Washington, D.C., and dropped the letter off at the White House gate. Nixon aide Bud Krogh (spelled "Bud Crow or Krog" in the discussion, settled on Krogh-style "Bud Ka") arranged the meeting, which happened at noon. Elvis brought a Colt .45 pistol in a display case as a gift, discussed counterculture, the Beatles and drugs, and received a narcotics badge. The hosts note the famous photo was kept quiet until Jack Anderson's column the following year and a Chicago newspaper report led to the National Archives photo becoming its most requested image, with about 8,000 requests in a week. They also mention two films about the meeting and Elvis's drug use.

segments.title: Introduction to the Elvis and Nixon photo
segments.summary: Hosts introduce the episode on the famous Elvis Presley and Richard Nixon meeting, mention Photoshop versions of the photo, and note a film about the story.

segments.title: Elvis's trip to Washington and the letter
segments.summary: After a Christmas argument with his father Vernon and his wife, Elvis flies to Washington, D.C., then to Los Angeles, and back. He writes a letter to Nixon offering service and asking for federal agent credentials, which is dropped at the White House gate. He visits the Federal Bureau of Narcotics himself while staying in a hotel.
topics: Elvis obsession with law enforcement badges

segments.title: Meeting arranged with Bud Krogh and the Oval Office talk
segments.summary: Nixon aide Bud Krogh, an Elvis fan, gets the letter and persuades Haldeman to arrange the meeting. Elvis arrives at noon with a Colt .45 in a display case, talks with Nixon about counterculture, the Beatles and drugs, and asks for a narcotics badge, which Krogh produces after lunch. Nixon and Elvis exchange gifts.

segments.title: Elvis's drug use and the photo's history
segments.summary: Hosts discuss Elvis's prescription and street drug use and a family anecdote about his doctors. They then cover Jack Anderson's column the following year, which did not catch on, and the later Chicago newspaper report that made the National Archives photo the most requested image, with about 8,000 requests in a week.

segments.title: Photo's later fame and Obama alien photo
segments.summary: The hosts note the photo was later surpassed as the most requested National Archives image by a photo of Obama meeting a lead singer of Corn, a joke about an alien-like figure.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts close the Short Stuff episode.
